---
title: "Building footprints in Argentina's barrios populares"
lang: en
---

*Annex to the main article. [Leer en español](index.qmd).*

Between surveys, Argentina’s *barrios populares* grow, become more densely
built, and emerge in new places. Open building footprints now cover the
whole country. They could help ReNaBaP field teams decide which
neighborhoods to revisit and where to look for settlements missing from the
registry.

These tutorials show researchers, journalists, local governments, and
community organizations how to examine the footprints in neighborhoods they
know. You can compare the outlines with satellite imagery to see which roofs
they capture and which they miss. Field surveys and residents’ knowledge can
help answer other questions, such as which buildings are homes and how many
families live in them.

- **[Python tutorial](tutorial_python_en.ipynb).** Download the data, count
  mapped buildings in each of the 6,467 ReNaBaP neighborhoods, and compare
  the footprints with satellite imagery at the former Club Planeadores in
  Los Hornos, La Plata. To run the tutorial,
  [download the notebook](tutorial_python_en.ipynb){download="tutorial_python_en.ipynb" data-noresolveinput="true"}
  and select **File > Upload notebook** in
  [Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/).
